prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The scene contains a seated person directly ahead, a small table with a chessboard between that person and the camera wearer, a cup to the person’s right, and seating and stairs around them; brighter values place the chessboard/table and the camera wearer’s visible hand nearest, roughly 0.3–0.8 m away, with the seated person about 1–1.5 m away and the cup at a similar depth to the person. The person remains centered and faces the camera wearer across the board, while the cup stays to the person’s right and slightly behind the board; the hand in frame 1 is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, and the board appears within reach of both people. Across the five frames, relative depths change little, though the camera shifts slightly and the near hand disappears after frame 1; in frame 5 the board occupies more of the lower-right view while the person is partly cropped at the top. The map makes foreground/background separation and approximate reach clearer than RGB, but it loses object boundaries and fine depth structure, over-brightens the tabletop, and gives no reliable metric scale, so metre estimates are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The map consistently isolates one person ahead and a cup to that person’s right, with the two separated laterally by roughly 0.6–1 m and both approximately 1–1.5 m from the camera wearer; it also isolates the camera wearer’s near hand only in frame 1. The person is centered above the table area and faces generally toward the camera wearer, while the cup remains right of the person and above/right of the board in RGB; the near hand overlaps and occludes part of the board in frame 1. Across frames 1–4 these masks remain in nearly fixed positions, while frame 5 crops much of the person and omits the cup, consistent with a rightward/downward view shift rather than clear object motion. Instance masks reveal occupied regions and occlusions more clearly than RGB, but the map misses the chessboard, table, sofa, and stairs, labels the table/board region as a suitcase in frame 3, changes the person’s colour in frame 5, and cannot itself provide dependable depth or facing direction.
descriptions.pose: The yellow skeleton places the seated person directly ahead, facing approximately toward the camera wearer with the head above the torso and the arms/hands gathered in front of the upper body; the magenta hand skeletons locate that person’s hands near the face/chest and, in frame 1, the camera wearer’s hand low-left near the chessboard. The seated person is roughly 1–1.5 m away, while the camera wearer’s detected hand is roughly 0.3–0.6 m away; the board lies below the person and appears within arm’s reach of both, although it is not drawn in this map. Across frames 1–4 the body remains centered with only small joint shifts, while frame 5 loses the body skeleton and retains only a cropped hand cluster near the upper-right, showing that the person becomes partly out of view rather than demonstrating a reliable retreat or turn. The pose map clarifies limb configuration, facing, reach, and hand overlap that are difficult to parse in RGB, but several joints float above the head, hand keypoints are dense or misplaced, lower-body geometry is unstable, and missing detections—especially in frame 5—make precise orientation and distance unreliable.
